newsitem.title: CANADA: FREESTYLE SKIING-HEMERY WINS MOGULS AFTER BRASSARD STUMBLES.
newsitem.headline: FREESTYLE SKIING-HEMERY WINS MOGULS AFTER BRASSARD STUMBLES.

text.p: Frenchman Thomy Hemery won the World Cup moguls competition Saturday as Olympic champion Jean-Luc Brassard never got close to the podium after stumbling out of the starting gate.
Hemery moved to second in the overall dual moguls points race by defeating Yugo Tsukita of Japan in the men's final. Petsch Moser of Switzerland won the bronze medal over Janne Lahtela of Finland.
American Garth Hager remained in the lead in the men's moguls standings despite finishing 16th Saturday.
Brassard, 24, who won the season-opening dual moguls in Tignes, France last month, misjudged the starter's commands, then tumbled out of the starting gate without one of his skis.
"I was ready to pounce like a tiger, but the controller took a little more time than I thought he would," said Brassard. "I didn't even ski one bump."
The mishap occurred in the round of 16 against Gota Miura of Japan who advanced to the next round. Brassard finished tied for ninth place with seven other skiers.

Marja Elfman of Sweden edged 1995 world moguls champion Candice Gilg of France in the women's event, while Minna Karhu of Finland defeated American Ann Battelle for the bronze to remain on top of the women's overall dual moguls points race.
